question: Do seven labels in Quezon’s flood advisory match river names in the BMB-DENR Atlas and same-named principal basins in DPWH Annex D-2?
purpose: Record bounded official source-name/province matches while keeping river channels, principal basins, advisory reaches, fish evidence and geometry distinct.

findings.evidence: Quezon Provincial Government General Flood Advisory No. 14 (7 August 2026) lists Bigol, Guinhalinan, Calauag, Pandanan, Sta. Lucia, Maapon and Tignoan as watercourses/river tributaries likely affected by that forecast.

The 2014 BMB-DENR Atlas Table 2 lists Bigol River (P-30, Ragay Gulf), Guinhalinan River (P-29, Ragay Gulf), Calauag River (O-27, Lamon Bay), Pandanan River (O-27, Lamon Bay), Sta. Lucia River (L-26/L-27, Lamon Bay), Maapon River (L-26, Lamon Bay) and Tignoan River (K-24, Lamon Bay), each under Region IV-A and Quezon.

DPWH Department Order 47 (2022), Annex D-2, separately lists same-named Region IV-A principal basins: Bigol row 92, 89 sq km; Guinhalinan row 93, 149 sq km; Calauag row 95, 163 sq km; Pandanan row 96, 154 sq km; Sta. Lucia row 97, 94 sq km; Maapon row 99, 201 sq km; and Tignoan row 102, 86 sq km.
supports: official principal-basin names and reported areas

crosswalks.decision: Add a separate research-only river-name lead; retain the DPWH principal basin as same-name context and do not merge basin extent into river geometry.

reuseAndLimitations: The BMB-DENR Atlas copyright page permits educational/non-profit reproduction with acknowledgement; it does not establish public-app or derived-database reuse.
The DPWH principal-basin table has no item-specific open-data license located; only minimal factual names and areas are retained.
The Atlas grid labels and outflow names are not route geometry; DPWH basin areas are not channel lengths or delineations.
The advisory is historical and not current hazard guidance.
No fish checklist, occurrence, current presence/absence, salinity, access, fishing rule, safety advice or geometry is established.
nextActions: Obtain permitted route-scale hydrography to determine whether each advisory label identifies the exact source-named river reach and how it relates to its same-name principal basin.
Search site-resolved fish surveys separately for all seven rivers; do not infer fish presence from waterbody identity or classification.
